data.reason: WAN NIC (vtnet0) transmit path is hung: dmesg shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link down/up cycles, netstat -i shows 48211 output errors on vtnet0, and traffic to the ISP gateway fails with ENOBUFS ("No buffer space available") while the interface reports status active. Four WAN reloads by the watchdog (rc=0 each, latest 03:25) did not clear it, and the watchdog has now hit its 12-reload/24h cap. The modem re-registered and reads OPERATIONAL, so a modem reboot won't help; only a full firewall reboot will reset the stuck driver. Maintainer is unreachable; per policy proceed if conditions hold.

data.cause: The WAN virtio driver's transmit path on gw.lan is wedged (repeated vtnet0 watchdog timeouts on queue 0), so no packets leave the firewall even though the interface is up with a valid DHCP lease and the cable modem reads OPERATIONAL.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP churn on the WAN NIC
netstat -i shows vtnet0 Oerrs=48211 while the LAN side vtnet1 has 0 errors
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 and ping -c 3 -n 8.8.8.8 fail at sendto with "No buffer space available", 100% loss, i.e. failure at transmission not beyond the ISP
arp -a -n shows the gateway 198.51.100.1 entry as (incomplete)/expired while the WAN address itself is still present
ifconfig vtnet0 shows UP RUNNING LOWER_UP status active with inet 198.51.100.27/24, so carrier/link is fine
cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 shows the lease valid to 2026/3/6, ruling out a DHCP lease problem
/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: outage_start 02:06 then reloads at 02:30, 02:40, 02:55, 03:25 all rc=0 with no recovery; 03:30 decision action=none reason=reload_cap (12 of max 12)
/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl plus modem-metrics.jsonl: modem rebooted and registration complete at 02:28, cm_status OPERATIONAL, min_snr ~37.7 dB at 03:30
netstat -rn shows the default route via 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0 intact; netstat -m shows 0 mbuf denial counters
data.recommendation: Reboot gw.lan to reset the hung vtnet0 transmit queue, since WAN/DHCP reloads cannot recover a wedged driver (12 reloads returned rc=0 without restoring connectivity); the maintainer was unreachable so firewall_reboot was requested and ran under stand-in conditions. After it comes back, verify ping to 198.51.100.1 succeeds and dmesg is free of vtnet0 watchdog timeouts; if the timeouts recur, treat the NIC as suspect hardware and replace it. Also update the watchdog so that hitting its 12-reloads-per-24h cap triggers an alert/escalation instead of silently doing nothing, and consider a driver-reset or reboot step at that point.
